summary: The zigzag result contains every node value, so producing it requires linear time. The deque-based breadth-first traversal matches that bound while using width-proportional auxiliary space.

optimality.argument: For an n-node tree, the returned level lists contain exactly n values, regardless of their alternating direction. Materializing those values requires Omega(n) time. The current traversal enqueues and dequeues every node once and inserts each value at one end of its level deque in O(1) time, giving O(n) total time and O(w) auxiliary space excluding the output.

replacement_checks.evidence: The required nested result explicitly contains all n node values, so it cannot be produced in o(n) time.
Each node enters and leaves the breadth-first deque once, and each value is appended once to a level deque.

The source-fidelity-verified examples cover alternating directions, a one-node tree, and an empty tree; black-box real-test execution verifies every existing ordinary check without inspecting its definition.
